tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Solvability of the generalized Dirichlet problem] Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0193 1. ch8:8.3\group ch08-generalized-solutions Assume (8.5), (8.6), and (8.8). For every $\varphi \in W^{1,2}(\Omega )$ and $g,f^i\in L^2(\Omega )$, the problem \[ Lu=g+D_if^i\quad \text{in }\Omega , \qquad u=\varphi \quad \text{on }\partial \Omega \] has a unique generalized solution.
Proof

\sketch Set $w=u-\varphi $ and absorb $L\varphi $ into $\hat g=g-c^iD_i\varphi -d\varphi $ and $\hat f^i=f^i-a^{ij}D_j\varphi -b^i\varphi $, reducing to zero boundary data. For sufficiently large $\sigma _0$, Lemma 8.4 makes the form of $L_{\sigma _0}=L-\sigma _0$ coercive. The equation is then a compact perturbation of the invertible operator $L_{\sigma _0}$ by Lemma 8.5. The Fredholm alternative and Corollary 8.2 give existence and uniqueness.

□
